title: Apple Watch Ultra 4 Unveils New Bezel‑Style Watch Face, Boosting Customization Options
body:
Apple has unveiled the next iteration of its flagship wearable, the Apple Watch Ultra 4, adding a distinctive bezel‑style complication that lets users frame their watch faces with a customizable ring of information. The new feature, exclusive to the Ultra line, joins a suite of enhancements—including fresh color palettes, additional fonts and a set of Ultra‑only watch faces—aimed at deepening personalization for the device’s adventure‑focused audience.

The bezel‑type complication is more than a cosmetic flourish; it transforms the outer edge of the screen into a functional data strip. Users can select from metrics such as depth, altitude, heart‑rate zones, or even a simple timer, which then scrolls around the perimeter of the display. Because the Ultra’s always‑on Retina LTPO OLED panel supports a 2‑second refresh rate, the information updates in near‑real time without draining the battery. Apple’s UI team has ensured that the bezel integrates seamlessly with existing complications, allowing the new ring to coexist with traditional dial‑based widgets or to replace them entirely for a cleaner look.

The addition reflects Apple’s broader strategy of differentiating the Ultra series from its standard Series line. While the Series 9 and SE models continue to emphasize health tracking and everyday convenience, the Ultra line is marketed toward athletes, divers, hikers and other users who demand rugged durability and specialized tools. The new Ultra‑only watch faces—such as “Dive,” “Alpine” and “Adventure”—already incorporate high‑contrast elements and larger tap targets suited for gloved operation. The bezel complication builds on this ethos by offering quick‑glance data that can be read without rotating the wrist, a practical advantage in low‑visibility environments like deep water or snowy terrain.

Industry analysts see the move as a response to growing competition in the premium smartwatch segment, where rivals such as Garmin and Suunto have long offered highly customizable data rings and modular interfaces. By integrating a similar concept into its own ecosystem, Apple not only narrows the feature gap but also keeps users locked into its broader suite of services, from Fitness+ workouts to the Apple Health data platform. The bezel’s configurability also opens new avenues for third‑party developers, who can now design watch faces that make use of the peripheral ring, potentially expanding the App Store’s smartwatch offerings.

Early adopters have praised the Ultra 4’s enhanced personalization options, noting that the bezel adds a sense of “mission control” to the wrist. However, some users voice concerns about the learning curve associated with configuring multiple complications and the potential for visual clutter. Apple’s onboarding flow includes a step‑by‑step tutorial that walks users through selecting and arranging bezel data, but the effectiveness of this guidance will likely be judged by how intuitively the feature integrates into daily wear.

Looking ahead, the bezel complication could set a precedent for future Apple Watch designs across all tiers. If the Ultra 4’s ring proves popular, Apple may roll out a scaled‑down version for the Series line, or even explore dynamic bezels that adapt based on activity context. For now, the Ultra 4 solidifies its position as the most customizable and rugged Apple Watch to date, offering enthusiasts a richer, more immediate way to monitor the metrics that matter most during their most demanding pursuits.
